'''R2-Q5''' was an [[R2-series astromech droid|R2-series]] [[astromech droid]]. Made by [[Industrial Automaton]], he served the [[Galactic Empire]] aboard the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]], performing maintenance and repair as needed. Like many Imperial astromechs, he was fitted with spy devices allowing [[human]] overseers to monitor personnel. He single-handedly thwarted a software infiltration of the Death Star II by the rogue [[assassin droid]] [[IG-88B]].<ref name="SWFC">{{ForceCollection|R2-Q5|star=3}}</ref> During the [[New Republic Era|era of the Resistance]], [[R0-GR]] included R2-Q5 in "[[droidography]]."<ref name="Droidography" />

==Biography==
===Servant of the Emperor===
{{Quote|In fact, plenty of astromechs served Imperial forces as mechanics, and some even worked as personal messengers for the Emperor himself. Take these guys, for example.|R0-GR writes about R4-I9 and R2-Q5|<ref name="Droidography" />}}
R2-Q5 was an [[R2-series astromech droid]] manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]]<ref name="CEUE" /> that served the [[Galactic Empire]] as one of the many [[droid]] [[Aide|attendant]]s to [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]]. The [[R-series]] [[astromech droid]] was primarily used for astrogation and data storage<ref name="SWFC" /> and patrolled the corridors of the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] [[superweapon]] carrying out maintenance and repair tasks. Many other Imperial astromechs fufilled the same role and were fitted with secret [[spy]] devices to allow [[human]] [[overseer]]s to monitor personnel.<ref name="CEUE" /> On one occassion, R2-Q5 single-handedly thwarted the [[assassin droid]] [[IG-88B|IG-88's]] attempted software infiltration of the [[Death Star]].<ref name="SWFC" />

[[File:R2-Q5-Jerrjerod-Hangar-ROTJ.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=Moff Tiaan Jerjerrod marches past a row of four black-uniformed Imperial officers, including Mianda, in a hangar on the Death Star II. In the background, R2-Q5 is visible at the rear of the hangar.|R2-Q5 (second from right) was stationed on the Death Star II.]]
In [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> during the [[Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]], the Death Star was still under construction over the [[moon]] [[Endor]] in the [[Endor system]]. When the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] arrived on board the superweapon to increase speed of production, R2-Q5 stood at the back of a group of Imperial personnel led by [[Moff]] [[Tiaan Jerjerrod]] in the [[hangar]] where Vader's [[shuttle]], [[ST 321]], landed.<ref name="ROTJ" /> He<ref name="Droidography" /> was also present in a larger group of droids<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> in [[Hangar 272]]<ref name="BattleStations">{{EncyclopediaCite|Battle Stations of the Empire and the First Order}}</ref> when Palpatine himself later landed on the station.<ref name="ROTJ" />

===Battle of Endor and beyond===
Not long after the [[Emperor]]'s arrival, the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] attacked the Death Star, having been fooled by Palpatine into beliving its weaponry was not yet operational.<ref name="ROTJ" /> During the battle, R2-Q5 performed duties for the Alliance instead of the Empire<ref name="GalacticFiles" /> and was present in a portion of the battle station's [[Command Sector (North)|Command Sector North]] where a rebel [[CR90 corvette]] crashed during the battle, leading to fighting in the Death Star's corridors between the Imperials and the [[corvette]]'s surviving crew as the latter sought a ship to escape on.<ref name="BFII">''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''</ref> The Alliance eventually succeeded in destroying the Death Star and [[Death|killing]] the Emperor.<ref name="ROTJ" />

The [[B1-series battle droid]] [[R0-GR]] later wrote about R2-Q5 and their fellow Imperial astromech [[R4-I9]] in a work he compiled and called a "[[droidography]]." R0-GR claimed that just from looking at the two astromechs' paint jobs he could tell that the pair was nothing that trouble.<ref name="Droidography" />

==Characteristics==
R2-Q5 had [[Gender|masculine programming]]<ref name="Droidography" /> and [[Color|black]] and bronze paneling with a black [[sensor]]. He was also equipped with a magnetic fault sensor, motorized [[Limb|legs]], a heat exhaust, a [[powerbus cable]] for tread,<ref name="CEUE" /> and an array of "quick repair" appendages that could swiftly contract into hidden compartments.<ref name="GalacticFiles" /> The droid stood 1.09 [[meter]]s (three [[foot]], seven inches) tall.<ref name="CEUE" /> The astromech had above average intelligence but below average strength and speed, with especially low diplomatic skills and fighting abilities. He was not [[Force-sensitive]].<ref name="GalacticFiles" />

==Behind the scenes==
R2-Q5 first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] and was first identified in [[canon]] by this name in the [[Wikipedia:Gashapon|gacha]] toy ''[[Star Wars Pullback Droid]]''. In the reference book ''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'', the title states that many droids like him are fitted with secret [[spy]] devices, it does not specify whether R2-Q5 specifically is in fact fitted with these.

===LEGO===
{{Quote|Make it quick. I'm up to my optical lenses in repair work, and if it doesn't get done today then… I dunno, something'll happen. Who has time to listen to consequences? My assistant really picked a day to play hooky. Think you could find that lazy lout for me and tell him to get his seat-warmer in gear?|R2-Q5|<ref name="LEGOSaga">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]''</ref>}}
In the non-canon animated series ''[[LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales]]'', R2-Q5 appeared during a flashbackto the [[Clone Wars]] in the episode "[[Crisis on Coruscant]],"<ref name="CoC">{{DroidTales|Crisis on Coruscant}}</ref> which aired on [[August 24]], [[2015]]<ref name="SW Twitter">{{Twitter|starwars|status/635941658606051328|Star Wars|date=24-08-2015|quote=Gather your younglings. LEGO Droid Tales Episode 2: Crisis on Coruscant airs tonight at 9:00pm on @DisneyXD!|archivedate=20190723162302}}</ref> In the flashback, R2-Q5 is depicted as serving the [[Executive Separatist Council]] on the [[planet]] [[Geonosis]] and is present at a meeting of the council in the [[Stalgasin hive]] where the captive [[protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]] is being forced to work as a waiter. C-3PO's companion [[R2-D2]] sneaks up behind R2-Q5 and smashes a rock of his dome, pulling him through a doorway, and then swapping out their paneling to disguise himself in black. R2-D2 initially forgets to swap out his dome, but returns to R2-Q5 and completes the disguise before [[Mission to Recover the Republic's Battle Plans|infiltrating]] the meeting.<ref name="CoC" />

R2-Q5 also appears in [[LEGO]] form as a character in the non-canon [[2015]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'' in which he is unlocked by completeing the bonus level "Trouble over [[Taul]]."<ref name="LEGOTFA">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''</ref> In the [[2022]] sequel ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'', R2-Q5 can be found in [[Bunker 01]] of the [[Resistance base]] on the planet [[D'Qar]] where he'll complain to the player in [[binary]] that he is busy with repair work and ask them to locate his missing [[R2-Q5's assistant|assistant]], who the droid consisders useless. If the player accepts the quest, which is titled "Not the Sharpest Tool in the Box," then R2-Q5 thanks them and gives them a [[datalog]] to deliver to the assistant, displaying a [[hologram]] of his appearance. Once the player finds the assistant in [[Bunker 04]], he reads the datalog, commenting that R2-Q5 clearly is not happy with him and some of the message got pretty personal. The mission is then complete and R2-Q5 is unlocked as a purchasable character to play as.<ref name="LEGOSaga" />
